entities.title: Declare the minimum Rust version
entities.summary: Cargo.toml admits any toolchain with edition 2021, but the code uses standard-library methods added much later.
entities.expected: A toolchain the manifest admits builds the crate, or Cargo refuses it up front with a clear message (Cargo's rust-version key).
entities.observed: Cargo.toml has edition = "2021" (Rust 1.56 or later) and no rust-version; src/ops.rs calls u32::is_multiple_of and src/zones.rs Option::is_none_or, which Rust's release notes date to 1.87 and 1.82, so an older toolchain fails mid-compile.

origin.description: No rust-version key; found while documenting the folder.

entities.details: The two call sites were checked in the code; the versions in which those methods became stable come from Rust's release notes and were not checked by building with older toolchains.

entities.title: State the conformance profiles the crate claims
entities.summary: VERSIONING.md requires each library to state, in its README and its package metadata where possible, the specification versions and the conformance profiles it supports; the Rust README and Cargo.toml state the versions only.
entities.expected: The README (and Cargo.toml's description where it fits) names the profiles of spec §2 the crate claims (core-civil, global-instant, zoned, ...), as VERSIONING.md and implementations/README.md ask.
entities.observed: README.md names utv/1.0, utv-result/1.0 and utv-text/1, and Cargo.toml's description utv/1.0; neither names a conformance profile.

origin.description: Implementation versions: "Each library MUST state ... which specification versions ... and which conformance profiles it supports."
